# env
- `.env.example` and environment variables must accurately reflect platform/service requirements — e.g., iOS and Android use separate client IDs from Google Cloud Console and must not be conflated into a single misleading variable. Confidence: 0.8
- When updating an environment variable's value in `.env`, must also update the same value in `.env.example` simultaneously to keep both files in sync. Confidence: 0.85
- Expects ALL env files across the project (root `.env`, `backend/.env`, `mobile/.env` / `mobile/.env.production`) to be kept in sync with their `.env.example` templates in both directions — when asked to sync env files ("sync semua env, hapus yang sudah tidak terpakai"), the agent should copy any vars present in the template but missing from `.env`, remove vars no longer used, and fix template variable names that no longer match actual code usage (e.g., `EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` → `EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID`, matching `useGoogleAuth.ts`). "Unused" is judged by actual source-code usage (grep for `process.env` / config reads, plus deployment docs/config), not by file-diff guessing or stale doc references; the final state is verified with an automated key-set comparison across all env files before declaring done. Confidence: 0.85
- Uses a single shared Supabase instance across all environments (development, local, and production) — `DATABASE_URL`/`DIRECT_URL` are identical everywhere with no environment-isolated fallback; the user noted this as an FYI during Vercel debugging, signaling that migrations must be run manually and non-destructively — the user manages schema changes manually via the Supabase Dashboard rather than via automated build-time migration or Prisma CLI. Consistent with the free-tier hosting preference. Confidence: 0.8
- Prefers env template files (`.env.example`) kept as short as possible — strip "unnecessary comments", keep only terse one-line explanations for non-obvious values, and remove prose/example blocks (e.g., a ~20-line commented CORS JSON) that already live in the docs, leaving a pointer to the doc instead. Reducing line count is an explicit goal ("reduce lines file .env.example"). Confidence: 0.75
- Prefers env files structured for "high maintainability" by grouping variables into clearly labeled sections classified by domain/service (e.g., Database · Supabase · Auth & app · Google · Cloudflare R2 · Email; Backend API · Supabase Realtime · Google Sign-In) with section header comments. Confidence: 0.75
- Actively eliminates redundancy/duplication across env templates: a section duplicated in another file (e.g., a Mobile/Expo section in the root `.env.example` that also lives in `mobile/.env.example`) should be removed rather than kept in both, and variables read nowhere in the code (e.g., `EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID`/`_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID` resolved from `app.json`) should be dropped — with the agent verifying kept keys map to real code usage and both templates stay consistent. Confidence: 0.75
- Env templates must live in exactly ONE canonical location: per-package, sitting next to the `.env` file they produce — and each package's copy target must be the env filename its own framework/loader actually reads, not a uniform `.env`: backend → `.env` (`ConfigModule.forRoot()` with no `envFilePath` reads only `.env`, so `.env.local` is silently ignored), mobile → `.env.local` (Expo/Metro loads `.env`, then `.env.local`, then `.env.<mode>`, and `.env.local` is the git-ignored dev file already in use — safer for prod since `.env.production` is loaded after and wins). README/setup must therefore show `cp backend/.env.example backend/.env` and `cp mobile/.env.example mobile/.env.local`, each annotated with why that target; telling newcomers to use `.env` for mobile would create two conventions (`.env` for newcomers vs `.env.local` for maintainers). No root `.env.example` at all. Rationale the user accepted: the `.env` files are loaded per-package at runtime (dotenv reads cwd, Metro/Expo reads the app root), so a root-only template has no runtime "home", always has to be split by hand on copy, and drifts from the package template. When offered "per-package" vs "root-only", chose per-package. A `cp .env.example .env` step for "root tooling" must be dropped when nothing in the repo actually loads a root `.env`. Confidence: 0.8
- Approves the agent generating internal/random secrets itself instead of supplying them — when the agent proposed to generate `JWT_SECRET` and `CRON_SECRET` on its own (256-bit hex via `openssl rand -hex 32` or `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`), the user simply answered "ya, tolong lanjut". The distinction is: values the agent can produce itself (random app secrets) it should generate and write straight into the git-ignored `.env`, while third-party credentials (Supabase service_role/JWT secret, R2, SMTP, OAuth client keys) must come from the user. Confidence: 0.55

- Type-check verification for mobile changes: the `mobile` package's `lint` script runs `tsc --noEmit`, invoked from the monorepo root as `pnpm --filter mobile lint` (pnpm workspace) — this is the verification command after editing mobile files (e.g., `mobile/app/(auth)/*.tsx`), alongside grep checks for now-unused styles/identifiers. Confidence: 0.7

- When populating a `.env` from its template, the user works one service section at a time ("mulai dari supabase dulu" — Supabase first) rather than filling every section in one pass, and expects the agent to autonomously fill the values that are derivable from the repo (e.g., reuse the public `SUPABASE_URL` / anon key already present in `mobile/.env.local`, rewrite DB usernames to the actual project ref) while leaving values it cannot derive as clear placeholders plus precise instructions on where the user can obtain them (Supabase Dashboard paths), only ever writing them into the git-ignored `.env`. Confidence: 0.6

- When creating third-party API tokens/keys for the project, the user issues them with broad scope instead of least privilege — the Cloudflare R2 token as **Admin Read & Write** (which can also create/delete buckets) and the Resend key as **full access** ("aku beri full access"), even right after the agent recommended the narrower option (`Object Read & Write` scoped to the bucket / `Sending access`). The agent should accept the credential as given, finish the setup and verification, and mention the least-privilege alternative only as an optional non-blocking note — never withhold verification or demand a narrower token first. Confidence: 0.6

- Deliberately skips optional integration config while finishing env setup — the Expo push token was deferred ("expo access token belum dulu btw") and a blank optional value that degrades gracefully (push skipped, email skipped) is an acceptable final state. The agent should report the remaining optional key once, note the graceful-degradation behavior, and move on rather than pressing for it or treating it as blocking. Confidence: 0.55

- For local web Google Sign-In, the mobile app's `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_ORIGIN` (used as the OAuth `redirect_uri`) must be a loopback http origin — `http://localhost:8081` — and registered verbatim as an Authorized redirect URI (and JavaScript origin) on the Web OAuth client. Google rejects `http://` non-loopback hosts: a LAN IP like `http://192.168.x.x:8081` (or a literal `<LAN-IP>` placeholder copied from the template) triggers `Error 400: invalid_request` / "doesn't comply with Google's OAuth 2.0 policy for keeping apps secure" (`Detail permintaan: redirect_uri=http://<LAN-IP>:8081`). Because `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` are inlined by Metro at build time, changing it requires restarting Metro with `--clear`. Confidence: 0.65

- Operates a SINGLE-environment setup: the deployed (Vercel production) environment variables should simply be made identical to the current local `backend/.env` contents, because "cuma ada 1 environment" (there is only one environment). Treats local-and-prod sharing the same values as the intended model rather than maintaining a separate production env set with its own diverging/deliberate overrides — when a deploy fails, aligning prod env to the local `.env` verbatim is the expected resolution path. The agent should still call out any value that genuinely must differ for the platform to work (e.g., `APP_ENV=production`, serverless DB `connection_limit=1`) and get confirmation rather than silently introducing prod-only values. Confidence: 0.7

- Supabase DB config: on a network without IPv6, the direct connection host `db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432` is unreachable (`P1001`). Use the IPv4 **session pooler** for `DIRECT_URL` (`aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`, user `postgres.<ref>`) — `prisma migrate` goes through it — while runtime `DATABASE_URL` keeps the transaction pooler (`:6543`, `?pgbouncer=true`). Verify any new DB config by running `pnpm exec prisma migrate status` (direct path) and a `SELECT 1` through a Prisma Client built with `DATABASE_URL` (pooler path). Confidence: 0.6
